The change in log-odds of remission for each one-year increase in patient age is **−0.0795** (SE 0.0263; 95% CI −0.131 to −0.028; p≈0.002). Equivalently, the odds ratio is exp(−0.0795) ≈ 0.924 (95% CI 0.877–0.972), i.e., each additional year of age is associated with ~7.6% lower odds of remission, holding BMI and gender constant.

Context: Remission was defined as Efficacy == "PR" (partial response; SD and PD = non-remission; no CR present). Logistic regression remission ~ Age + BMI + Gender was fit by MLE (statsmodels Logit) on the 80 clean rows (41/80 events); the model converged cleanly with no separation.
